Aaron — thanks, and great meeting earlier. Attached is our first-pass Performance Acceptance Matrix (nebula_benchmark_matrix.csv) and a lightweight runbook for the team (runbook_k6_scenarios.yaml). Summary below so procurement has a clear yes/no acceptance checklist: 

- Acceptance criteria (baseline):
  * Model: open-llama-13b (quantized variant recommended for cost).
  * Throughput: 300 QPS sustained on typical request mix (70% short chat, 30% long chat) for 30m window.
  * Tail latency: p95 <= 360ms, p99 <= 900ms for generation endpoints at 1k token max.
  * Cold-start: model variant swap (fallback) should not exceed 1.5s added latency under burst.
  * Error rate: < 0.5% client-visible 5xx across the run.

- Observability artifacts we will hand over after each run: per-request traces (Zipkin-compatible IDs), per-token cost breakdown (CSV), per-route latency heatmaps, and KV/prefix cache hit-rate summaries.

- Run cadence proposal:
  * Day 0 — smoke + single-VM baseline (dry run with 15m warmup).
  * Day 1 — scaled sustained run to target concurrency (30m sustained).
  * Day 2 — stress/failover scenarios (node failover / model fallback).

I'll note Monica will coordinate schedule with your infra team; Vivek will own the Kubernetes/job templates and k6 harness configs.

--
maya_srinivasan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: nebula_benchmark_matrix.csv (stub), runbook_k6_scenarios.yaml (stub)

Aaron / team — some quick technical clarifications and the command snippets we'll run inside the preprod account. Important assumptions: a) inference instances will be m90x2 equivalent, b) we will pin model weights to quantized-8bit variant for the run, c) prefix caching will be enabled for repeat prompt templates.

Planned verification steps (runbook highlights):
- Environment prep: ensure no background batch jobs, sync clocks, and disable autoscaler for controlled runs.
- Metrics: collect per-GPU utilization, process RSS, request/response histograms (prometheus histograms exported to our collection pipeline).
- k6 scenarios: 
  * checkout_flow: 60% of traffic, 1–2 prompts, avg 120 tokens; target 200 QPS.
  * search_suggestion: 30% of traffic, short prompt, p95 <= 120ms expected.
  * long_form: 10% of traffic, up to 600 tokens, target p95 <= 700ms.
- Failure injection: terminate one worker pool mid-run, observe fallback to warm standby.

Command example (snippet):
  k6 run runbook_k6_scenarios.yaml --out json=nebula_run_day1.json

Artifacts we will upload to Drive after each run: nebula_run_day{n}.json, perf-heatmap.png, logs_{timestamp}.tar.gz.

Vivek

Subject: Mutual action plan: Nebula Retail benchmarking window and acceptance rules

Hi Priya / Aaron — thanks for the quick questions. Below is the mutual action plan (MAP) we propose; please confirm or flag changes by EOD Friday so we can schedule infra windows next week.

MAP Summary:
- Assumptions: 1 user session = 1 connection / average concurrency factor 2.5 (we will size for 2x safety margin).
- Acceptance flow:
  1) Day 0 smoke — run baseline to validate config. If smoke fails (p95 > 2x target), stop and diagnose.
  2) Day 1 acceptance run — 30m sustained at target QPS. If p99 exceeds target by more than 25%, we automatically trigger a remedial run with tuned batching/quantization. The remedial run must be scheduled within 48 hours.
  3) Day 2 resilience tests — simulated worker termination and model fallback. Failure during resilience tests does not block purchase but will add a conditional remediation milestone in the SOW.
- Deliverables to Nebula after each run: full k6 JSON, per-token-cost CSV (route annotated), Prometheus scrape snapshots, and a short one-page readout with recommended configuration changes.
- Sign-off criteria: Day 1 run meets p95 and p99 targets and error rate <0.5%. If remedial run still misses p99, procurement may accept with a 90-day remediation SLA (TBD).

Proposed dates: smoke on 2028-04-18, acceptance run on 2028-04-19, resilience on 2028-04-20. Please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Onboarding
Redwood Inference
